title: Affliction's Faded Form Draws Nigh
description: Affliction's Faded Form Draws Nigh in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 329, “Affliction, God's Angel”, where the book credits them to the N. Y. Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Af-flic-tion's fad-ed form draws nigh, With wrin-kled brow and down-cast eye; With sack-cloth on her bo-som spread, And ash-es scat-tered o'er her head.

lines: With wrinkled brow and downcast eye;
With sackcloth on her bosom spread,
And ashes scattered o'er her head.
But deem her not a child of earth;
From heaven she draws her sacred birth;
Beside the throne of God she stands
The messenger of love, she flies
To train us for our sphere, the skies;
And onward as we move, the way
Becomes more smooth, more bright the day.
Her weeds to robes of glory turn,
Her looks with kindling radiance burn;
And from her lips these accents steal, —
"God smites to bless, he wounds to heal!"

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
